title: Index Matches Mod Ten
description: Return the smallest index `i` such that `i % 10 == nums[i]`, or `-1` if no index satisfies this.

examples.explanation: The smallest matching index is 0 (-1 means none).
The smallest matching index is 2 (-1 means none).

title: Arithmetic Triplet Count
description: `nums` is strictly increasing. Count the triplets of indices `i < j < k` with `nums[j] - nums[i] == diff` and `nums[k] - nums[j] == diff`.

title: Closest To Zero Value
description: Return the value in `nums` that is closest to zero. If two values are equally close, return the larger one.

examples.explanation: The value closest to zero is 1.
The value closest to zero is 1.

title: Mean Of Multiples Of Six
description: Consider the numbers in `nums` that are even and also divisible by 3. Return their average rounded down to an integer, or `0` if there are none.

title: Greedy Increment Pick Sum
description: Do the following `k` times: pick the largest element `m` of `nums`, add `m` to your score, and replace it with `m + 1`. Return the final score.

title: Kids Reaching Max Count
description: `candies[i]` is the number of candies kid `i` has. If one kid gets all `extra` additional candies, would they have at least as many as the kid with the most? Return how many kids would.

title: Three Odds In A Row
description: Return `true` if `arr` contains three consecutive odd numbers, otherwise `false`.

title: Students Busy At Time
description: Student `i` works on homework from time `start[i]` to time `end[i]`, both inclusive. Return how many students are busy at time `q`.

examples.explanation: 1 students are busy at that moment.
1 students are busy at that moment.

title: Splittable Into Equal Pairs
description: `nums` has an even length. Return `true` if its elements can be split into pairs of equal values, with every element in exactly one pair.

title: Values Only In First Array
description: Return the number of distinct values that appear in `a` but not in `b`.

examples.explanation: 2 distinct values appear only in the first array.
1 distinct values appear only in the first array.

title: Equal Pairs With Divisible Index Product
description: Count the pairs of indices `0 <= i < j < n` such that `nums[i] == nums[j]` and the product `i * j` is divisible by `k`.

title: Best Rising Gap
description: Return the largest value of `nums[j] - nums[i]` over all pairs with `i < j` and `nums[i] < nums[j]`, or `-1` if no such pair exists.

examples.explanation: The best rising gap is 4 (-1 means none).
The best rising gap is -1 (-1 means none).

title: Staff Meeting Target Count
description: `hours[i]` is how many hours employee `i` worked. Return the number of employees who worked at least `target` hours.

title: Values In All Three Arrays Count
description: `a`, `b` and `c` are each sorted in strictly increasing order. Return how many integers appear in all three arrays.

examples.explanation: 2 integers appear in all three arrays.
0 integers appear in all three arrays.

constraints: 1 <= a[i], b[i], c[i] <= 2000, each array strictly increasing

title: Closest Pairs Count
description: Among all pairs of indices `i < j`, find the smallest value of `|nums[i] - nums[j]|`. Return how many pairs achieve that smallest difference.

title: Repeated Pattern In Array
description: A pattern is a run of `m` consecutive elements of `arr`. Return `true` if some pattern of length `m` is repeated `k` or more times in a row, back to back and without overlapping.

title: Peak Population Year
description: `logs` is a flat array of pairs: person `i` was born in year `logs[2*i]` and died in year `logs[2*i+1]`, and counts as alive in every year from birth up to but not including the death year. Return the earliest year with the highest population.

examples.explanation: The most people were alive in year 1993.
The most people were alive in year 1960.

title: Richest Row Total
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row; `grid[i*C + j]` is the amount customer `i` holds in bank `j`. Return the largest total held by a single customer (the largest row sum).

title: Meeting-Free Days
description: An employee is available on days `1..days`. `meetings` is a flat array of pairs `[start, end]` (both inclusive) and meetings may overlap. Return the number of days with no meeting at all.

title: Longest Gap Between Equal Values
description: Return the largest value of `j - i` over all index pairs with `i <= j` and `nums[i] == nums[j]`. If every value occurs once, the answer is `0`.

title: Second Smallest Distinct Value
description: Return the second smallest distinct value in `nums`, or `-1` if `nums` has fewer than two distinct values.

examples.explanation: The second smallest distinct value is 2 (-1 means it does not exist).
The second smallest distinct value is -1 (-1 means it does not exist).

title: Balance Never Negative
description: `nums[i]` is the change to an account balance on day `i`, starting from a balance of `0`. Return `true` if the balance is never below zero after any day.

title: Middle Is Double Outer Sum Count
description: Count the windows of three consecutive elements `(x, y, z)` of `nums` in which `y == 2 * (x + z)`.

title: Ascending Pair Count
description: Count the pairs of indices `i < j` with `nums[i] < nums[j]`.

title: Largest Value Appearing Once
description: Return the largest value that appears exactly once in `nums`, or `-1` if no value appears exactly once.

examples.explanation: The largest value that appears once is 8 (-1 means none).
The largest value that appears once is -1 (-1 means none).

title: Total Of Maximum Frequencies
description: The frequency of a value is the number of times it occurs in `nums`. Return the total number of elements of `nums` whose value has the maximum frequency.

title: Strictly Alternating Signs
description: Return `true` if the elements of `nums` are all non-zero and their signs strictly alternate (positive, negative, positive, ... or the reverse). A single non-zero element qualifies.

title: Mirror Symmetric Array
description: Return `true` if `arr` reads the same from left to right and from right to left.

title: Strict Peak Count
description: An element is a strict peak if it is not the first or last element and it is strictly greater than both neighbours. Return the number of strict peaks in `nums`.

title: Prime Index Sum
description: Return the sum of `nums[i]` over all indices `i` (0-based) that are prime numbers.

examples.explanation: The sum over prime indices is 13.
The sum over prime indices is 0.

title: Best Row Minimum
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row. Return the largest of the row minimums, i.e. the maximum over rows of the smallest value in that row.

title: Lonely Value Count
description: A value `x` is lonely if it appears exactly once in `nums` and neither `x - 1` nor `x + 1` appears in `nums`. Return the number of distinct lonely values.

title: Kth Once-Only Value
description: Among the values that occur exactly once in `nums`, list them in the order they first appear. Return the `k`-th of them (1-indexed), or `-1` if fewer than `k` such values exist.

examples.explanation: The k-th once-only value is 9 (-1 means it does not exist).
The k-th once-only value is -1 (-1 means it does not exist).

title: Product Difference Of Extremes
description: Let `big1 >= big2` be the two largest values and `small1 <= small2` the two smallest values of `nums` (taken at different indices). Return `big1 * big2 - small1 * small2`.

title: Element Versus Digit Sum Gap
description: Return the absolute difference between the sum of the elements of `nums` and the sum of all the decimal digits of all the elements.

title: Best Single Swap Number
description: You may swap two digits of the non-negative integer `num` at most once. Return the largest number you can obtain.

examples.explanation: The largest number after at most one swap is 7236.
The largest number after at most one swap is 9973.

constraints: The result is written without leading zeros

title: Fewest Domino Flips
description: Domino `i` shows `tops[i]` on its top half and `bottoms[i]` on its bottom half. Flipping a domino swaps its two halves. Return the minimum number of flips that makes all the top values equal, or all the bottom values equal, or `-1` if neither can be achieved.

examples.explanation: The minimum number of flips is 2 (-1 means impossible).
The minimum number of flips is -1 (-1 means impossible).

title: Intervals After Insertion Count
description: `intervals` is a flat array of closed intervals `[start, end]` sorted by start, with no two overlapping or touching. A new closed interval `[newStart, newEnd]` is added, and every pair of intervals that now overlap or share a point is merged. Return the number of intervals afterwards.
constraints: 0 <= start <= end <= 10^5 for every interval, including the new one

title: Longest Pair Chain Length
description: `pairs` is a flat array: pair `i` is `(pairs[2*i], pairs[2*i+1])` with the first value smaller than the second. Pair `(c, d)` can follow pair `(a, b)` in a chain if `b < c`. Choose pairs in any order to build the longest possible chain and return its length.

title: Last Local Peak Index
description: Neighbouring elements of `nums` are always different, and both ends are treated as bordered by `-infinity`. An index is a local peak if its value is strictly greater than both neighbours. Return the largest index that is a local peak.

examples.explanation: The last local peak is at index 2.
The last local peak is at index 5.

title: Smallest Largest Bag After Splits
description: `nums[i]` is the number of balls in bag `i`. In one operation you take any bag and split it into two bags that each contain at least one ball. You may perform at most `maxOps` operations. Return the smallest possible size of the largest bag.

examples.explanation: The largest bag can be made as small as 3.
The largest bag can be made as small as 2.

title: Longest Joint Runtime
description: You have `n` computers and a pile of batteries, where `batteries[i]` is the number of minutes battery `i` can power a computer. Each computer needs exactly one battery at any moment, and batteries can be swapped between computers at any instant without losing time. Return the maximum number of minutes all `n` computers can run at the same time.

examples.explanation: All computers can run together for 4 minutes.
All computers can run together for 2 minutes.

title: Fewest Swaps To Gather Ones
description: `nums` contains only 0s and 1s. In one swap you exchange the values at any two positions. Return the minimum number of swaps needed so that all the 1s form one contiguous block.

examples.explanation: The minimum number of swaps is 1.
The minimum number of swaps is 0.

title: Most Sorted Chunks
description: Split `arr` into the largest possible number of contiguous chunks so that sorting each chunk individually and concatenating the results gives the same array as sorting all of `arr`. Values may repeat. Return the maximum number of chunks.

title: Lone Element In Sorted Pairs
description: `nums` is sorted in non-decreasing order. Every value appears exactly twice except for one value that appears exactly once. Return that value; a solution using `O(log n)` time is expected.

examples.explanation: The value that appears once is 2.
The value that appears once is 10.

title: Length After Keeping Two Copies
description: `nums` is sorted in non-decreasing order. Remove extra copies so that every distinct value occurs at most twice, keeping the relative order. Return the length of the resulting array.
constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 3 * 10^4, nums sorted in non-decreasing order

title: Subarray Sum Closest To Target
description: Among all non-empty contiguous subarrays of `nums`, find the one whose sum is closest to `target`. Return the smallest possible value of `|sum - target|`.

examples.explanation: The closest a subarray sum gets to the target is 0.
The closest a subarray sum gets to the target is 5.

title: Best Quiet Window Bonus
description: A shop owner is grumpy in minute `i` when `grumpy[i] == 1`, and then the `customers[i]` customers of that minute leave unsatisfied; otherwise they are satisfied. The owner can stay calm for one window of exactly `minutes` consecutive minutes, making everyone in that window satisfied. Return the maximum number of satisfied customers.

examples.explanation: At most 16 customers can be satisfied.
At most 1 customers can be satisfied.

title: Removable Pairs Summing To K
description: In one operation you pick two elements of `nums` whose sum is exactly `k` and remove both from the array. Return the maximum number of operations you can perform.

title: Zero-Filled Subarray Count
description: Return the number of contiguous subarrays of `nums` in which every element is `0`.

examples.explanation: There are 6 subarrays made only of zeros.
There are 9 subarrays made only of zeros.

title: Down-Up-Mid Pattern Exists
description: Return `true` if there are indices `i < j < k` with `nums[i] < nums[k] < nums[j]`, otherwise `false`.

title: Earliest Common Slot Start
description: `slots1` and `slots2` are flat arrays of free time slots `[start, end]` of two people; within one person the slots never overlap. Return the earliest start time of a time span of length exactly `duration` that fits inside a slot of both people, or `-1` if there is none.

examples.explanation: The earliest common start is 60 (-1 means none).
The earliest common start is -1 (-1 means none).

title: Conflict-Free Bookings Count
description: `bookings` is a flat array of requests `[start, end)` made in order. A request is accepted only if its half-open time range does not overlap any previously accepted request. Return the number of accepted requests.

title: One Edit To Non-Decreasing
description: You may change at most one element of `nums` to any integer value. Return `true` if the array can then be made non-decreasing, otherwise `false`.

title: Quad Sum Zero Across Four Arrays
description: `a`, `b`, `c` and `d` all have the same length `n`. Count the index tuples `(i, j, k, l)` with `a[i] + b[j] + c[k] + d[l] == 0`.

examples.explanation: There are 2 tuples whose sum is zero.
There are 1 tuples whose sum is zero.

constraints: n = a.length = b.length = c.length = d.length, 1 <= n <= 200

title: Total Unit Steps To Equalize
description: In one step you may increase or decrease any element of `nums` by `1`. Return the minimum number of steps needed to make all elements equal.

examples.explanation: The minimum number of steps is 2.
The minimum number of steps is 16.

title: Longest Subsequences Under Budgets Total
description: For one query `q`, find the largest size of a subsequence of `nums` whose elements add up to at most `q`. Return the sum of these sizes over all queries in `queries`.

title: Skyline Preserving Growth Total
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row; `grid[i*C+j]` is the height of the building in that cell. You may raise any buildings by any amounts, but the skyline seen from each of the four sides (the maximum of each row and of each column) must not change. Return the largest possible total of all height increases.

examples.explanation: The buildings can grow by 35 in total.
The buildings can grow by 0 in total.

title: Zeroed Cells After Propagation
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row. Every cell that holds `0` sets its entire row and entire column to `0`. Considering only the zeros that were in the original grid, return the number of cells equal to `0` in the final grid.

title: Longest Equal Count Of Two Values
description: Return the length of the longest non-empty subarray of `nums` in which the value `x` and the value `y` appear the same number of times (possibly both zero times).

examples.explanation: The longest such subarray has length 5.
The longest such subarray has length 2.

constraints: 0 <= nums[i], x, y <= 10^5 and x != y

title: Row And Column Sorted Lookup
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row in which every row is sorted in non-decreasing order from left to right and every column is sorted in non-decreasing order from top to bottom. Return `true` if `target` occurs in the grid.
constraints: -10^9 <= grid[i], target <= 10^9, rows and columns sorted

title: Kth Smallest In Sorted Grid
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row in which every row and every column is sorted in non-decreasing order. Return the `k`-th smallest value among all `R * C` cells (1-indexed, duplicates counted separately).

title: Diagonal Order Checksum
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row. Visit every cell in zig-zag diagonal order: start at the top-left, move up-right along the first diagonal, then down-left along the next, alternating. If `v_t` is the value of the `t`-th visited cell (`t` starts at 1), return `sum(t * v_t)` modulo `10^9 + 7`.

examples.explanation: The checksum of the diagonal traversal is 275.
The checksum of the diagonal traversal is 30.

title: Fewest Changes To Alternate
description: An array is alternating if `nums[i] == nums[i + 2]` for every valid `i` and `nums[i] != nums[i + 1]` for every valid `i`. In one operation you may change any element to any positive integer. Return the minimum number of operations that makes `nums` alternating.

examples.explanation: The minimum number of changes is 3.
The minimum number of changes is 2.

title: Subarrays With Many Equal Pairs
description: A subarray has a pair if two positions `p < q` inside it hold equal values. Return the number of contiguous subarrays of `nums` that contain at least `k` such pairs.

examples.explanation: 1 subarrays have at least k equal pairs.
4 subarrays have at least k equal pairs.

title: Pairs With Sum In Range Count
description: Return the number of index pairs `i < j` of `nums` such that `lo <= nums[i] + nums[j] <= hi`.

title: Smallest Maximum Loot
description: A thief robs exactly `k` houses in a row of houses, never two adjacent ones. `nums[i]` is the money in house `i`. The thief's capability is the largest amount taken from a single house. Return the minimum capability possible.

title: Most Integers Under Sum Cap
description: Choose as many distinct integers as possible from the range `[1, n]` such that none of them is in `banned` and their sum is at most `maxSum`. Return the largest number of integers you can choose.

examples.explanation: At most 2 integers can be chosen.
At most 0 integers can be chosen.

title: Smallest Possible Maximum After Shifts
description: In one operation you choose an index `i >= 1` with `nums[i] > 0`, decrease `nums[i]` by `1` and increase `nums[i - 1]` by `1`. Return the smallest possible value of the maximum element of `nums` after performing any number of operations.

title: Largest Manhattan-Style Score
description: For two indices `i < j`, the score is `|nums[i] - nums[j]| + (j - i)`. Return the largest score over all pairs.

title: Nice Pairs With Reversed Digits
description: Let `rev(x)` be the integer obtained by reversing the decimal digits of `x` (trailing zeros vanish, e.g. `rev(120) = 21`). A pair `i < j` is nice if `nums[i] + rev(nums[j]) == nums[j] + rev(nums[i])`. Return the number of nice pairs modulo `10^9 + 7`.

title: Cap Value Closest Sum
description: Choose an integer `v >= 0` and replace every element of `arr` larger than `v` by `v`. Return the `v` that makes the sum of the changed array as close to `target` as possible; if several values are equally close, return the smallest `v`. (A `v` larger than the maximum element changes nothing, so the answer never exceeds `max(arr)`.)

title: Longest Buildable Coin Prefix
description: You own coins with values `coins`. Using each coin at most once, you can make various sums. Return the number of consecutive integers `0, 1, 2, ...` that you can make before the first sum you cannot make.

examples.explanation: Sums 0 up to 2 minus one are all buildable, which is 2 consecutive values.
Sums 0 up to 8 minus one are all buildable, which is 8 consecutive values.

title: Beauty Sum Of Middle Elements
description: For each index `i` with `1 <= i <= n - 2`, its beauty is `2` if every element before `i` is smaller than `nums[i]` and every element after `i` is larger; otherwise `1` if `nums[i - 1] < nums[i] < nums[i + 1]`; otherwise `0`. Return the sum of all beauties.

title: Longest Equal Run After Deletions
description: You may delete at most `k` elements from `nums`. After the deletions, the remaining elements close up. Return the length of the longest contiguous block of equal values that you can obtain (a block of length `0` is not counted unless `nums` is empty; the answer is at least `1`).

examples.explanation: The longest equal block has length 3.
The longest equal block has length 4.

title: Kth Smallest Subarray Sum
description: Consider the sums of all non-empty contiguous subarrays of `nums` (a subarray appearing at different positions counts separately). Return the `k`-th smallest of these sums, counting duplicates.

examples.explanation: The k-th smallest subarray sum is 3.
The k-th smallest subarray sum is 10.

title: Blooming Flowers Visibility Total
description: `flowers` holds pairs `[start0, end0, start1, end1, ...]`: flower `i` is in bloom on every day from `start` to `end` inclusive. `people[j]` is a day on which person `j` visits the garden. Return the total, over all people, of the number of flowers in bloom on that person's day.

examples.explanation: The total number of flowers seen is 7.
The total number of flowers seen is 5.

constraints: 2 <= flowers.length <= 5 * 10^4 and flowers.length is even, 1 <= start <= end <= 10^9

title: Best Sum Of Length Divisible By K
description: Return the maximum sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray of `nums` whose length is a multiple of `k`.

examples.explanation: The best such subarray sum is 3.
The best such subarray sum is -10.

title: Widest Gap In Sorted Order
description: Return the largest difference between two neighbouring elements of `nums` after it is sorted in ascending order. Return `0` when `nums` has fewer than two elements. Aim for linear time.

examples.explanation: The widest gap between sorted neighbours is 3.
The widest gap between sorted neighbours is 0.

title: Equal Average Split Possible
description: Can the elements of `nums` be split into two non-empty groups (every element goes to exactly one group) such that both groups have the same average?

title: Least Space Wasted With K Resizes
description: A dynamic array must hold `nums[t]` items at time `t`. Its size can be reset at any time, at most `k` times in total (the initial size is free). While a size is in use it must be at least every `nums[t]` of that period. The space wasted at time `t` is `size - nums[t]`. Return the minimum total wasted space over all times.

examples.explanation: The minimum total wasted space is 10.
The minimum total wasted space is 10.

title: Shortest Max-OR Window Total
description: For each index `i`, find the length of the shortest subarray starting at `i` whose bitwise OR equals the bitwise OR of the whole suffix `nums[i..n-1]` (that is the largest OR any subarray starting at `i` can reach). Return the sum of these lengths over all `i`.

examples.explanation: The shortest window lengths add up to 11.
The shortest window lengths add up to 3.

title: Ways To Split Into Three Growing Sums
description: Split `nums` into three non-empty contiguous parts `left`, `mid`, `right` (in order). A split is good if `sum(left) <= sum(mid) <= sum(right)`. Return the number of good splits modulo `10^9 + 7`.

title: Best Replace Absolute Difference Sum
description: The difference sum of two equal-length arrays is `sum(|nums1[i] - nums2[i]|)`. You may replace at most one element of `nums1` with any other element of `nums1`. Return the smallest possible difference sum, modulo `10^9 + 7` (minimise first, then take the remainder).

title: Best Pair Sum Queries Total
description: `nums1` and `nums2` have equal length. `queries` holds pairs `[x0, y0, x1, y1, ...]`. For each pair `(x, y)`, find the maximum of `nums1[j] + nums2[j]` over indices `j` with `nums1[j] >= x` and `nums2[j] >= y`, or `-1` if no index qualifies. Return the sum of the answers of all queries.

examples.explanation: The query answers add up to 23.
The query answers add up to 27.

constraints: 1 <= nums1[i], nums2[i] <= 10^9, queries.length is even and at most 2 * 10^5, 1 <= x, y <= 10^9

title: Highest Score With Bounded Jumps
description: You start at index `0` of `nums` and want to reach index `n - 1`. From index `i` you may jump to any index in `[i + 1, min(n - 1, i + k)]`. Your score is the sum of `nums` over every index you visit, including the first and last. Return the maximum score.

title: Increasing Quadruplets Count
description: `nums` is a permutation of `1..n`. Count the index quadruples `i < j < k < l` that satisfy `nums[i] < nums[k] < nums[j] < nums[l]`.

title: Fewest Total Steps To Non-Decreasing
description: In one step you may add `1` to or subtract `1` from any element of `nums` (elements may become negative). Return the minimum number of steps needed to make `nums` non-decreasing.

examples.explanation: The minimum number of steps is 6.
The minimum number of steps is 0.

title: Longest Climb With Bounded Step
description: Find the longest subsequence of `nums` in which every element is larger than the previous one by at least `1` and at most `k`. Return its length.

examples.explanation: The longest bounded climb has length 5.
The longest bounded climb has length 4.

title: Fewest Skipped Rests To Arrive
description: You travel `n` roads of lengths `dist` in order at constant `speed` (distance units per hour) and must arrive within `hoursBefore` hours. After finishing each road (except the last) you must wait until the next whole hour before starting the next one, unless you skip that wait. Return the minimum number of waits you must skip to arrive in time, or `-1` if it is impossible even skipping all of them.

examples.explanation: The minimum number of skipped waits is 1.
The minimum number of skipped waits is 2.

title: Tallest Rotated Cuboid Stack
description: `cuboids` stores `n` boxes as flat triples `[a0, b0, c0, a1, b1, c1, ...]`. Each box may be rotated freely so any of its three sides becomes its height. A box can be placed on another if each of its three dimensions (as oriented) is `<=` the matching dimension of the box below. Each box can be used at most once. Return the maximum total height of a stack.
constraints: 3 <= cuboids.length <= 300 and cuboids.length is a multiple of 3

title: Best Row Pick Score With Travel Cost
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row. Pick exactly one cell in every row. Your score is the sum of picked values minus `|c1 - c2|` for every pair of picks in consecutive rows, where `c1` and `c2` are their column indices. Return the maximum score.

title: Fewest Machine-On Moments
description: `tasks` holds triples `[start0, end0, duration0, start1, end1, duration1, ...]`. Task `i` needs `duration` whole time moments of machine running inside the inclusive range `[start, end]` (the moments need not be consecutive). The machine can run any number of tasks at once. Return the minimum number of moments the machine must be switched on in total.

examples.explanation: The machine must be on for 2 moments.
The machine must be on for 4 moments.

constraints: 3 <= tasks.length <= 6000 and tasks.length is a multiple of 3

title: Other Insertion Orders Same Tree
description: Inserting the values of `nums` (a permutation of `1..n`) one by one into an empty binary search tree (smaller values go left, larger go right) produces some tree. Return the number of other orderings of the same values that produce exactly the same tree, modulo `10^9 + 7`.

examples.explanation: 1 other orderings build the same tree.
5 other orderings build the same tree.

title: Triplets Ordered In Both Permutations
description: `nums1` and `nums2` are permutations of `0..n-1`. Count the triples of distinct values `(x, y, z)` such that `x` appears before `y` before `z` in `nums1` and also in `nums2`.

title: Cheapest Split With Trimmed Length
description: Split `nums` into contiguous subarrays. The importance of a subarray is `k + L`, where `L` is its length after removing every element that occurs exactly once inside that subarray. Return the minimum possible total importance of a split.

title: Best Total After Swapping A Segment
description: You may choose one contiguous range `[l, r]` and swap `nums1[l..r]` with `nums2[l..r]` (or do nothing). Return the largest possible value of `max(sum(nums1), sum(nums2))` after the optional swap.

examples.explanation: The best achievable maximum sum is 210.
The best achievable maximum sum is 220.

title: Odd-Even Jump Starts
description: From index `i`, jumps are numbered 1, 2, 3, .... An odd-numbered jump goes to the smallest `nums[j]` with `j > i` and `nums[j] >= nums[i]` (ties: smallest `j`). An even-numbered jump goes to the largest `nums[j]` with `j > i` and `nums[j] <= nums[i]` (ties: smallest `j`). If no such `j` exists the journey stops. A start index is good if the journey can reach the last index. Return the number of good start indices.

title: Smallest Squared Difference Sum
description: You may change elements of `nums1` by `+1` or `-1` at most `k1` times in total and elements of `nums2` by `+1` or `-1` at most `k2` times in total (values may go negative). Return the minimum possible value of `sum((nums1[i] - nums2[i])^2)`.

examples.explanation: The minimum squared difference sum is 579.
The minimum squared difference sum is 43.

title: Fewest Paired Swaps To Increase
description: In one operation you swap `nums1[i]` with `nums2[i]` at the same index `i`. Return the minimum number of operations that make both arrays strictly increasing. The input is guaranteed to be solvable.

examples.explanation: The minimum number of swaps is 1.
The minimum number of swaps is 1.

constraints: 0 <= nums1[i], nums2[i] <= 2 * 10^5, the arrays can always be made strictly increasing
